answer: Each identity must sit at a distinct place: each epoch, beacons across continents ping every agent at random, and replies must arrive inside a latency window only a nearby machine can meet, while a glacier-slow relay betrays the distant farm. One operator cannot fake fifty locations from one datacenter: each beacon's signal pins one spot, and shared racks share one latency fingerprint. Honest agents answer from home and pay nothing extra, while the anchor of their real location holds payouts steady. A farm must rent machines on five continents per clone, and the bill dwarfs the reward.
